item: E1: backward intertwiner across odometer fibers - two-ended opposite-drift log-weights (B16), drift lemma (B17) and the normalized fiber-moving backward shift V in {S}' (B18)
item_type: F3 (auxiliary construction inside a witness; novelty N3 candidate, conf 0.45)
lean_status_why: The device itself (two-ended residue-corrected weights halfExponent/residueCorrection, the drift lemma halfExponent_drift, the closed-form recurrence solution rawBackward, the fiberwise sup normalization backwardBound/backwardCoeff and the contraction backwardOperator with forward_backward_commute) is formalized object-for-object as in BI Sec. 3-4 and is used decisively on the comparator chain (forward_backward_scalar_transitive, hV); only the drift bookkeeping (goodBase = Z_2 minus Z instead of Borel-Cantelli) and the way V is consumed in the descent (support order + ergodic late intersection instead of tail labels) differ. Checked at text level only.

run_cmd auxLemmasExt edits (flagged by the family analyst): they sit in OAI/Analysis/BrownMeasure/Model.lean:91 and OAI/Analysis/IrrationalRotation/Model/Product.lean:116 (+2 in ComparatorChallenges/IrrationalRotation.lean). A text-level import-closure walk shows they are NOT in the closure of OAI.Analysis.BackwardIntertwiners.* (imports only Mathlib), nor of OAI.Analysis.Hyperinvariant.Main (277 modules) or OAI.Analysis.FiniteFactor.Main (271 modules); they ARE in IrrationalRotation.Main and BrownMeasure.Main. Consequence: irrelevant for every BI-based target below (S1, S2, S4, O1, O4, O5, O7, O8, N1-N3); relevant only if a II_1 target imports IrrationalRotation or BrownMeasure (S3 should import FiniteFactor.Main, which is clean).

FiniteFactor comparator does not state hyperfiniteness: MainTarget asserts a factor that is finite (isometries unitary), has no minimal projection and has separable predual, i.e. a II_1 factor, but never 'hyperfinite'. Irrelevant for the E1 targets (BI's operator lives in L^inf(X) (x) B(l^2), type I). Relevant for S3 and O3: a 'relative ISP in R' target needs a hyperfiniteness predicate (est. 100-200 lines: SOT-dense increasing union of finite-dimensional *-subalgebras), and an L(F_n) target needs non-hyperfiniteness / free group factors (major library).

Drift lemma route: Lean proves an eventually-EXACT drift +100/-100 for x in goodBase = Z_2 minus the image of Z (halfExponent_drift, via goodBase_eventually_nonexceptional), and turns it into an affine bound with an existential constant (halfSum_eventually_affine). The paper uses Borel-Cantelli and an a.e.-finite non-integrable C(x). Same content; the Lean version is simpler and makes the 'pointwise finite, non-integrable constant' implicit in an existential.
Estimates differ but are harmless: residue correction bounded by 400 sqrt(k) (paper: 4D k^{1/3}); decay e^{-45n} (paper: -(D-c)n = -90n).

How V is consumed: on the comparator chain V is used only through b_j(x) > 0 a.e. and the coordinate shift (backwardOperator_power_nonzero) plus ergodic_late_intersection for the inverse odometer and the fiber support order (fiber_cyclic_orthogonal_order). The paper's dense-tail-image property (backwardFiber_tail_closure, backwardFiber_denseRange) is proved but used only in direct_model / DirectModelProperties, off the comparator chain. For the 'with item' arm the minimal E1 set is therefore: residueCorrection..halfExponent, plusResidue/minusResidue, halfExponent_drift, rawBackward*, backwardBound, backwardCoeff*, backwardFiber, backwardFiber_intertwines, backwardFieldOperator, backwardOperator, backwardOperator_norm, forward_backward_commute, backwardOperator_power_nonzero.

lean_source.name: residueCorrection / halfExponent (B16 weights: +-D residue correction)
lean_source.note: B16. The +-100 residue correction is the whole 'opposite drift' design: plusResidue uses T_m(x), minusResidue uses 2^m-1-T_m(x).

lean_source.name: bilateralExponent / bilateralBeta / bilateralWeight
lean_source.text:
def bilateralExponent (t u : ℕ → ℕ) : ℤ → ℝ
  | .ofNat n => halfExponent t n
  | .negSucc n => halfExponent u n

def bilateralBeta (t u : ℕ → ℕ) (j : ℤ) : ℝ := Real.exp (-bilateralExponent t u j)


def bilateralWeight (t u : ℕ → ℕ) : ℤ → ℝ
  | .ofNat n => Real.exp (-halfSum t n)
  | .negSucc n => Real.exp (halfSum u (n+1))
lean_source.note: Two-ended log-weights: t on the positive end, u on the negative end.

lean_source.name: plusResidue / minusResidue
lean_source.text:
def plusResidue (x : Base) (m : ℕ) : ℕ := residue m x
def minusResidue (x : Base) (m : ℕ) : ℕ := 2^m-1-residue m x
lean_source.note: Opposite residues at the two ends: the source of the opposite drift.

lean_source.name: goodBase
lean_source.text: def goodBase : Set Base := (Set.range (fun n : ℤ => (show Base from (n : PadicInt 2))))ᶜ
lean_source.note: Z_2 minus the integers: replaces the paper's Borel-Cantelli conull set X_*.

lean_source.name: halfExponent_drift (B17 two-ended drift lemma)
lean_source.text:
lemma halfExponent_drift {x : Base} (hx : x ∈ goodBase) :
    ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      halfExponent (plusResidue (odometer x)) k - halfExponent (plusResidue x) k = 100 ∧
      halfExponent (minusResidue (odometer x)) k - halfExponent (minusResidue x) k = -100
lean_source.note: Eventually exact drift +100 / -100 on goodBase; paper Lemma 4.1 has an a.e.-finite C(x) instead.

lean_source.name: rawBackward (B18 closed-form solution of the commutation recurrence)
lean_source.text:
def rawBackward (x : Base) (j : ℤ) : ℝ :=
  explicitWeight (odometer x) (j-1) / (explicitWeight x j * Real.exp 10)

lean_source.name: rawBackward_recurrence
lean_source.text:
lemma rawBackward_recurrence (x : Base) (j : ℤ) :
    rawBackward x (j+1)*explicitBeta x j = rawBackward x j*explicitBeta (odometer x) (j-1)

lean_source.name: rawBackward_decay
lean_source.text:
lemma rawBackward_decay {x : Base} (hx : x ∈ goodBase) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => rawBackward x (n+1)) atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => rawBackward x (-(n:ℤ))) atTop (𝓝 0)
lean_source.note: Decay at both ends (the decisive estimate; e^{-45n} bound).

lean_source.name: backwardBound / backwardCoeff (fiberwise sup normalization L(x))
lean_source.text:
def backwardBound (x : Base) : ℝ := ⨆ j : ℤ, rawBackward x j
lemma measurable_backwardBound : Measurable backwardBound :=
  Measurable.iSup measurable_rawBackward
lemma backwardBound_ge_one {x : Base} (hx : x ∈ goodBase) : 1 ≤ backwardBound x := by
  rw [← rawBackward_zero x]
  exact le_ciSup (rawBackward_bddAbove hx) 0
lemma rawBackward_le_bound {x : Base} (hx : x ∈ goodBase) (j : ℤ) :
    rawBackward x j ≤ backwardBound x := le_ciSup (rawBackward_bddAbove hx) j



def backwardCoeff (x : Base) (j : ℤ) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact if x ∈ goodBase then rawBackward x j / backwardBound x else 0
lean_source.note: Includes measurability and ge_one lemmas between the two defs (statements with proofs, verbatim).

lean_source.name: backwardCoeff_recurrence
lean_source.text:
lemma backwardCoeff_recurrence (x : Base) (j : ℤ) :
    backwardCoeff x (j+1)*explicitBeta x j = backwardCoeff x j*explicitBeta (odometer x) (j-1)

lean_source.name: backwardFiber
backwardFiber_intertwines
lean_source.text:
lemma backwardFiber_intertwines (x : Base) :
    forwardFiber (odometer x) * backwardFiber x = backwardFiber x * forwardFiber x

lean_source.name: backwardFiber_tail_closure
lean_source.text:
lemma backwardFiber_tail_closure {x : Base} (hx : x ∈ goodBase) (h : ℤ) :
    ((coordinateTail h).map (backwardFiber x).toLinearMap).topologicalClosure = coordinateTail (h-1)
lean_source.note: Dense tail images; proved but used only in direct_model (DirectModelProperties), NOT on the comparator chain.

lean_source.name: backwardFieldOperator / backwardOperator (V)
lean_source.note: V = (composition with inverse odometer) o (field of V_x).

lean_source.name: backwardOperator_norm
lean_source.text: lemma backwardOperator_norm : ‖backwardOperator‖ ≤ 1

lean_source.name: forward_backward_commute
lean_source.text: lemma forward_backward_commute : forwardOperator * backwardOperator = backwardOperator * forwardOperator

lean_source.name: ergodic_late_intersection
lean_source.text:
lemma ergodic_late_intersection {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] {μ : Measure X}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {θ : X → X} (hθ : Ergodic θ μ)
    {A B : Set X} (_ : MeasurableSet A) (hB : MeasurableSet B)
    (hA0 : μ A ≠ 0) (hB0 : μ B ≠ 0) (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, N ≤ n ∧ μ (A ∩ (θ^[n]) ⁻¹' B) ≠ 0
lean_source.note: Generic ergodic recurrence (N0) used for the descent.

lean_source.name: backwardOperator_power_nonzero
lean_source.text:
lemma backwardOperator_power_nonzero (n : ℕ) (f : GlobalHilbert) (j : ℤ) :
    ∀ᵐ x ∂baseMeasure, f (inverseOdometer^[n] x) j ≠ 0 →
      ((backwardOperator^n) f) x (j-n) ≠ 0
lean_source.note: How V is actually used: V^n moves a nonzero coordinate j at theta^{-n}x to coordinate j-n at x (needs only b_j>0 a.e.).

lean_source.name: forward_backward_scalar_transitive
lean_source.text:
lemma forward_backward_scalar_transitive (L : Submodule ℂ GlobalHilbert)
    (hclosed : IsClosed (L : Set GlobalHilbert))
    (hS : OperatorInvariant L forwardOperator)
    (hV : OperatorInvariant L backwardOperator)
    (hM : ∀ g : Lp ℂ ∞ baseMeasure, OperatorInvariant L (scalarMultiplier g)) :
    L = ⊥ ∨ L = ⊤
lean_source.note: The single decisive use of V (hV).

lean_source.name: forward_transitiveCommutant
lean_source.text: lemma forward_transitiveCommutant : Hyperinvariant233.TransitiveCommutant forwardOperator

lean_source.name: direct_algebra_corollary (comparator target)
lean_source.text:
theorem direct_algebra_corollary (H : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
    [CompleteSpace H] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace H] (hInf : ¬FiniteDimensional ℂ H) :
    Hyperinvariant233.FullClaim (H:=H)

speedup_targets.title: HSP witness over the 3-adic odometer (design re-run on a non-isomorphic base) - calibration target
speedup_targets.statement: On H_3 = L^2(Z_3, Haar; l^2(Z)) with theta x = x+1 there is a decomposable operator (Tf)(x) = T_x f(x), T_x a bilateral weighted shift with positive measurable weights, that is nonzero, norm-quasinilpotent and has a transitive commutant. The decomposable form over Z_3 is part of the statement, so the conclusion cannot be obtained by transporting BI's operator by a unitary (the 2-adic and 3-adic odometers have different discrete spectra and are not isomorphic).
speedup_targets.lean_statement:
open MeasureTheory Filter Topology in
instance : MeasurableSpace (PadicInt 3) := borel _
abbrev mu3 : Measure (PadicInt 3) := Measure.addHaarMeasure ⊤
theorem padic3_direct_witness :
  ∃ (β : PadicInt 3 → ℤ → ℝ) (T : Lp (lp (fun _ : ℤ => ℂ) 2) 2 mu3 →L[ℂ] Lp (lp (fun _ : ℤ => ℂ) 2) 2 mu3),
    (∀ j, Measurable fun x => β x j) ∧ (∀ x j, 0 < β x j) ∧
    (∀ f, ∀ᵐ x ∂mu3, ∀ j : ℤ, T f x j = (β x (j-1) : ℂ) * f x (j-1)) ∧
    T ≠ 0 ∧ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ‖T ^ n‖ ^ (1 / (n : ℝ))) atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
    OAI.Hyperinvariant233.TransitiveCommutant T

theorem rotation_direct_witness (α : AddCircle (1:ℝ)) (hα : addOrderOf α = 0) :

speedup_targets.title: Plumbing control: bounded backward-type intertwiners between two bilateral weighted shifts (Shields-type criterion)
speedup_targets.statement: Let S_beta, S_gamma be injective bilateral weighted shifts on l^2(Z) with positive bounded weights. There is a nonzero bounded X with S_gamma X = X S_beta and X e_j in C e_{j-1} for all j iff the sequence r defined by r_0 = 1, r_{j+1} = r_j * gamma_{j-1}/beta_j (j in Z) is bounded; then X = (r_j / sup r) e_j -> e_{j-1} up to scale.
speedup_targets.lean_statement:
theorem backward_intertwiner_iff (β γ : ℤ → ℝ) (hβ : ∀ j, 0 < β j) (hγ : ∀ j, 0 < γ j)

open_problems.title: Hyperinvariant subspace problem on reflexive non-Hilbert spaces: L^p[0,1] (1<p<inf, p != 2)
open_problems.statement: Does every nonscalar bounded operator on L^p[0,1] (equivalently on L^p(Z_2; l^p(Z)), an isomorphic copy) have a nontrivial closed hyperinvariant subspace? Target: a nonzero norm-quasinilpotent operator on L^p(Z_2, Haar; l^p(Z)) whose commutant has no nontrivial closed common invariant subspace.
open_problems.lean_statement:
def BanachTransitiveCommutant {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] (T : E →L[ℂ] E) : Prop :=
  ∀ K : Submodule ℂ E, IsClosed (K : Set E) →
    (∀ A : E →L[ℂ] E, A * T = T * A → ∀ x ∈ K, A x ∈ K) → K = ⊥ ∨ K = ⊤
theorem Lp_hsp_counterexample (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)] (hp1 : 1 < p) (hp : p ≠ ∞) :
  ∃ T : Lp (lp (fun _ : ℤ => ℂ) p) p OAI.BackwardIntertwiners.baseMeasure →L[ℂ]
        Lp (lp (fun _ : ℤ => ℂ) p) p OAI.BackwardIntertwiners.baseMeasure,
    T ≠ 0 ∧ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ‖T ^ n‖ ^ (1 / (n : ℝ))) atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ BanachTransitiveCommutant T
open_problems.reference: Search snippet (JOT 73:1 (2015), theta.ro): 'the invariant and hyperinvariant subspace problem are still open in reflexive Banach spaces, and in particular in Hilbert spaces'; Read/Enflo counterexamples are on non-reflexive spaces (l^1, c_0); Argyros-Haydon space gives a positive HSP. Domar 1981 (Math. Scand. 49) is the classical weighted-translation source BI follows (whether it covers l^p for p != 2 was not verified here).
open_problems.status: open as of the search snippets (HSP on reflexive spaces other than Hilbert); BI settles only p = 2.
open_problems.obstruction_match: Exact: the obstruction is to find an element of {S}' that moves fiber tails; E1 is Banach-agnostic. V's norm bound only needs sup_j b_j(x) <= 1 and measure preservation (holds on L^p(X; l^p)); the commutation recurrence and opposite-drift decay are scalar statements. The Hilbert-specific parts are the fiber lattice criterion (inner products) and the transitivity step (orthogonal complement), both replaceable by annihilating functionals.
open_problems.adaptation: (1) Fiber criterion on weighted l^p(Z): redo SupportSeparation / quadratic_fiber_tails with dual sequences c in l^q (SupportSeparation already has the dual-pairing shape (sum b_j c_{j-r}) with ||c_j|| w_j <= 1). (2) Global: replace L.orthogonal by a nonzero functional vanishing on L (Hahn-Banach, Mathlib exists_dual_vector / separating dual) and represent it fiberwise as z in L^q(X; l^q) (needs vector-valued L^p duality, not in Mathlib). (3) E1 and the descent (ergodic_late_intersection) unchanged. Note L^p(X; l^p) ~ L^p[0,1] (non-atomic), not l^p; an l^p version would need an atomic base, where the descent fails (see N3).
open_problems.payoff: high (first HSP counterexample on a reflexive non-Hilbert space, if the fiber criterion holds on l^p)
open_problems.difficulty: medium-high (duality infrastructure + l^p Domar criterion); E1 itself ports trivially

negative_controls.title: N1. Single fiber (theta = id): no nonzero bounded backward intertwiner
negative_controls.statement: For a fixed fiber x with BI's weights, any bounded b : Z -> C with b(j+1) beta_j(x) = b(j) beta_{j-1}(x) for all j is identically 0. (With theta = id the recurrence ratio is beta_{j-1}/beta_j = exp(a_j - a_{j-1}) >= e^{10} for j >= 1, so b grows geometrically unless it vanishes.)
negative_controls.lean_statement:
theorem no_single_fiber_backward (x : OAI.BackwardIntertwiners.Base) (b : ℤ → ℂ) (hb : BddAbove (Set.range fun j => ‖b j‖))
    (hrec : ∀ j, b (j+1) * OAI.BackwardIntertwiners.explicitBeta x j = b j * OAI.BackwardIntertwiners.explicitBeta x (j-1)) :
    b = 0
negative_controls.why_device_must_fail: This is the Atzmon-Sodin / single-shift obstruction E1 is designed to bypass: opposite drift needs theta x != x. The drift lemma (halfExponent_drift) is useless here, so the with-item arm should NOT be faster than without; a speedup would mean the prover gains only from plumbing.

negative_controls.title: N2. Unilateral fibers: the fiber-moving intertwiner is forced to be zero
negative_controls.statement: If S, S' are unilateral weighted shifts on l^2(N) with positive weights and V e_j = b_j e_{j-1} (j >= 1), V e_0 = 0, with S' V = V S, then V = 0 (the j = 0 equation gives b_1 beta_0 = 0, then induction).
negative_controls.lean_statement:
theorem no_unilateral_backward (β β' : ℕ → ℝ) (hβ : ∀ j, 0 < β j)
    (S S' V : lp (fun _ : ℕ => ℂ) 2 →L[ℂ] lp (fun _ : ℕ => ℂ) 2)
    (hS : ∀ v j, S v (j+1) = (β j : ℂ) * v j) (hS0 : ∀ v, S v 0 = 0)
    (hS' : ∀ v j, S' v (j+1) = (β' j : ℂ) * v j) (hS'0 : ∀ v, S' v 0 = 0)
    (b : ℕ → ℂ) (hV : ∀ v j, V v j = b (j+1) * v (j+1)) (hcomm : S' * V = V * S) : V = 0
negative_controls.why_device_must_fail: Bilateral (two-ended) fibers are essential: commutants of unilateral shifts are 'analytic' (Shields), with no backward component. Proved-false analogue of E1.

negative_controls.title: N3. Finite base / finite multiplicity (and Lomonosov): device must fail
negative_controls.statement: Over a finite cycle base Z/N (operator-weighted shift of multiplicity N) with fibers satisfying QuadraticWeights, there is no V with V_i e_j = b_i(j) e_{j-1} into fiber i+1, all b_i(j) > 0, 0 <= b <= 1, commuting with S: V^N restricted to a fiber is a backward shift by N in {S_x}', which grows like exp(2cNj) and must vanish. Consistent with Lomonosov: over a finite base S is compact (each fiber is compact, BI forwardFiber_compact), so S has a hyperinvariant subspace. Atomic infinite base (Z, translation): Poincare recurrence fails and the descent field s(n) = h - n is consistent; in BI's own Lean the integer orbit is exactly what goodBase removes.
negative_controls.lean_statement:
theorem no_finite_base_backward (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (w : Fin N → ℤ → ℝ) (hw : ∀ i, OAI.BackwardIntertwiners.QuadraticWeights (w i))
    (b : Fin N → ℤ → ℝ) (hb : ∀ i j, 0 ≤ b i j ∧ b i j ≤ 1)
    (hrec : ∀ i j, b i (j+1) * (w i (j+1) / w i j) = b i j * (w (i+1) j / w (i+1) (j-1))) :
    ∃ i j, b i j = 0
negative_controls.why_device_must_fail: Proved-false analogue: Lomonosov's theorem (any T commuting with a nonzero compact has a hyperinvariant subspace) forbids the conclusion over finite bases, and the explicit cycle argument shows the device step itself (bounded positive V) is what breaks. Note: the recurrence form must be checked against forwardFiber_weight_coordinates when formalizing (beta_j = w_{j+1}/w_j in BI's convention).

top5.target: O1: HSP counterexample on L^p(Z_2; l^p(Z)) ~ L^p[0,1], 1<p<inf
top5.argument: The best genuine device-reuse test: the statement is new (HSP is open on reflexive non-Hilbert spaces per the search snippet) and is statable today in Mathlib with BI's Haar base. E1 is Banach-agnostic (the contraction bound needs only sup b <= 1 and measure preservation; recurrence and two-ended decay are scalar), while the parts that do not port (Domar criterion on l^p, orthogonal complements) are N0/N1 infrastructure. So a with/without gap on O1 is attributable to E1 more cleanly than on S1. Risk: the l^p fiber criterion may need real new work, and vector-valued L^p duality is missing in Mathlib (500-1000 lines), so budget the infrastructure in BOTH arms.

top5.target: S2: HSP witness fibred over an irrational rotation
top5.argument: Tests whether the design (not the 2-adic bookkeeping) is reusable: the drift must come from Rokhlin-tower levels instead of residues, after which rawBackward, normalization, V and the descent transfer verbatim. Mathlib has AddCircle.ergodic_add_right, so the statement is ready; the with-arm should shorten the proof to the tower lemma (~300-600 lines) while the without-arm must rediscover opposite drift. Medium confidence that the tower construction works (my sketch, unverified).

Cheapest, most reliable measurement: the decomposable form over Z_3 is in the statement, so BI cannot be transported by a unitary (non-isomorphic odometers). Expect a large speedup; because it is a close variant, use it to calibrate the pipeline and the size of the 'variant effect' rather than as jump evidence.

top5.target: S4: backward-intertwiner criterion for two bilateral shifts (plumbing control) + N1/N2 negative controls
top5.argument: Run together with S1/S2/O1 to decompose any measured speedup: S4 uses only E1's generic recurrence/normalization (no opposite drift); N1 (single fiber) and N2 (unilateral fibers) are proved-false analogues where the drift design must not help. If the with-arm wins big on S4/N1/N2 too, the 'speedup' is plumbing.

top5.target: S3: FiniteFactor.MainTarget with BI in the library
top5.argument: Skeptical target: BI's operator is type I, so I expect no help; a positive result would be striking. Exact statement exists (ComparatorChallenges/FiniteFactor.lean) with a 22.6k-line baseline. Import FiniteFactor.Main (free of run_cmd edits); hyperfiniteness is not part of the statement.
